customManagers.description: Update Ruby versions in GitHub Actions matrix entries (which the github-actions manager doesn't see), marked with a `# renovate: datasource=ruby-version depName=ruby` comment

packageRules.description: Applies ":preserveSemverRanges" to the custom manager above. See: https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/discussions/28090

Offer Ruby patch updates separately from minor ones. Otherwise a pinned 3.2.x is only offered the newest non-major Ruby (e.g. 3.4.x), which the next rule disables, so it never gets a 3.2 patch release

Only take patch updates for Ruby itself. CI Ruby versions are pinned per major.minor on purpose (e.g. 3.2 is the Ruby the OpenVox 8 agent ships, 4.0 is OpenVox 9's), so moving to a new minor or major is a deliberate change made by hand
Group Ruby patch updates, and the ruby/setup-ruby updates they depend on, into one PR per repository

Put ruby/setup-ruby in the same PR as Ruby patch updates. CI can only use a new Ruby once setup-ruby supports it, so a Ruby bump must never be merged ahead of the setup-ruby update it needs. The slug is `patch-ruby` because `separateMinorPatch` makes Renovate prefix the Ruby patch group's slug with `patch-`, and setup-ruby's updates must land on that same `renovate/patch-ruby` branch
setup-ruby is the code CI trusts to install Ruby, so give each release time to be checked before it's used. This must stay shorter than the ruby-version wait below

Hold Ruby a day longer than setup-ruby, so the setup-ruby release that supports it is already in the group PR when the Ruby bump arrives. ruby-lang.org gives only a release date, so this wait counts from midnight UTC; a release late in the UTC day can still arrive a few hours before setup-ruby support and fail CI until setup-ruby catches up
